reviews.review:
“Let’s make it clean” said every pixel pusher ever. Yawn

The designers ruined a pretty good app.  But they got to make lots of important stuff in figma and have lots of meetings about these oh so important, revolutionary changes. 

Nothing says good design like your users having to guess where you put features.

Fire the art director

Seriously Ternus. Clean house. This version of the camera app is embarrassing for everyone involved.

reviews.title: Dysfunctional and Bloated
reviews.review: Like most things updated with apple glass, the camera app has stopped functioning properly; the app stalls and freezes when trying to open it, various functions sometimes break if you manage to get the app open, and even if you get a photo despite the entire app breaking as you use it the photos often fail to save to the camera roll. I have more than enough storage free, and no other apps running. Just a once-perfectly adequate app made into a shoddy mess because, for some reason, everything needs to look like it’s made out of glass lenses.

reviews.title: Expensive but the app keeps on crashing. Not worth it
reviews.review:
I was initially excited about this app, especially the feature that allows you to remove unwanted objects or distractions from photos. That capability is exactly why I decided to subscribe, despite the relatively high monthly cost.
Unfortunately, my experience has been extremely disappointing. After completing just one edit, the app consistently crashes and fails to save any progress. It becomes unusable almost immediately, which makes the subscription feel unjustified. Paying $12.99 plus tax for a service that does not function reliably is frustrating.
If AI tools are going to be a core feature, they should at least perform consistently and deliver the value users are paying for. At the very least, the app should be stable enough to complete basic edits without crashing

reviews.title: Sherman To VSCO 2026
reviews.review:
VSCO really changed my life this past year.

Not even on some hype, just being real… it brought me back to why I started creating in the first place. The process, the feeling, the intention behind every image.

I picked up a camera in 2011 with no real direction, just passion. Somewhere along the way I got caught up in everything else, but VSCO helped me reconnect with that original energy while also pushing me forward into a new era of creativity, community building.

From building my visual identity to being recognized, championed and licensed on the platform, even seeing my work exist in real spaces it’s been a full circle moment.

I know there’s a lot of conversation happening right now around AI lab and where things are going, but for me it’s always been about how we use the tools authentically!

I’m grateful to be part of a platform that continues to evolve and open new doors for creators like me.

This is just the beginning. Thank you team VSCO!! -SHERMAN T

reviews.title: Remember to create
reviews.review:
VSCO was never popular where i grew up. I used it for couple years as a cloud storage for photos that i held on very dearly. during the quarantine i started using it more, and i think as everyone else i took a free online course about photo editing. one day i woke up and my phone was blown with notifications, my photos were being liked and reposted like a little crazy, ngl it made my day, and most importantly i’ve had the opportunity to meet wonderful people, one of whom i’ve been amazing friends for years. And i was even encouraged to learn professional photography, i even pursued a career in photography “””didn’t get that exactly””” but i had a beautiful opportunity when i was in Europe. Moving forward years, i live in a place i never thought i will, i’m doing things that are afar from photography.
Among all the noise, VSCO reminds me to create, it’s my peaceful space, and it’s the keeper of my most precious memories and people.

reviews.title: Expensive but the app keeps on crashing. Not worth it
reviews.review:
I was initially excited about this app, especially the feature that allows you to remove unwanted objects or distractions from photos. That capability is exactly why I decided to subscribe, despite the relatively high monthly cost.
Unfortunately, my experience has been extremely disappointing. After completing just one edit, the app consistently crashes and fails to save any progress. It becomes unusable almost immediately, which makes the subscription feel unjustified. Paying $12.99 plus tax for a service that does not function reliably is frustrating.
If AI tools are going to be a core feature, they should at least perform consistently and deliver the value users are paying for. At the very least, the app should be stable enough to complete basic edits without crashing

reviews.title: Sherman To VSCO 2026
reviews.review:
VSCO really changed my life this past year.

Not even on some hype, just being real… it brought me back to why I started creating in the first place. The process, the feeling, the intention behind every image.

I picked up a camera in 2011 with no real direction, just passion. Somewhere along the way I got caught up in everything else, but VSCO helped me reconnect with that original energy while also pushing me forward into a new era of creativity, community building.

From building my visual identity to being recognized, championed and licensed on the platform, even seeing my work exist in real spaces it’s been a full circle moment.

I know there’s a lot of conversation happening right now around AI lab and where things are going, but for me it’s always been about how we use the tools authentically!

I’m grateful to be part of a platform that continues to evolve and open new doors for creators like me.

This is just the beginning. Thank you team VSCO!! -SHERMAN T

reviews.title: Remember to create
reviews.review:
VSCO was never popular where i grew up. I used it for couple years as a cloud storage for photos that i held on very dearly. during the quarantine i started using it more, and i think as everyone else i took a free online course about photo editing. one day i woke up and my phone was blown with notifications, my photos were being liked and reposted like a little crazy, ngl it made my day, and most importantly i’ve had the opportunity to meet wonderful people, one of whom i’ve been amazing friends for years. And i was even encouraged to learn professional photography, i even pursued a career in photography “””didn’t get that exactly””” but i had a beautiful opportunity when i was in Europe. Moving forward years, i live in a place i never thought i will, i’m doing things that are afar from photography.
Among all the noise, VSCO reminds me to create, it’s my peaceful space, and it’s the keeper of my most precious memories and people.

reviews.title: UPDATE: 2/17/26 Weird Import Feature for Video
reviews.review:
After being able to communicate with a real person and not AI, I was able to get my Pro Membership expedited to the paid version to have access to the Film 02 and other features. I was also able to finally sign into the app after having may server issues. 

Weird way of importing video. You have to already have something in your Studio to have the option to import video. Otherwise it will only have the photos option. That’s a terrible way to function. Once you add something to your studio, you’ll have the option to add video. I deleted everything from the Studio to see if I could replicate it. Doing so only gave me the option for importing photos. When I added a photo to the Studio, it worked for video again. PLEASE give the option for video and video whether you have something in your Studio or not.

reviews.title: Sherman To VSCO 2026
reviews.review:
VSCO really changed my life this past year.

Not even on some hype, just being real… it brought me back to why I started creating in the first place. The process, the feeling, the intention behind every image.

I picked up a camera in 2011 with no real direction, just passion. Somewhere along the way I got caught up in everything else, but VSCO helped me reconnect with that original energy while also pushing me forward into a new era of creativity, community building.

From building my visual identity to being recognized, championed and licensed on the platform, even seeing my work exist in real spaces it’s been a full circle moment.

I know there’s a lot of conversation happening right now around AI lab and where things are going, but for me it’s always been about how we use the tools authentically!

I’m grateful to be part of a platform that continues to evolve and open new doors for creators like me.

This is just the beginning. Thank you team VSCO!! -SHERMAN T

reviews.title: Masters of Marketing Comms & Cons
reviews.review:
This dev shop is adept at coming up with clever marketing terms for features that are mere gimmicks. A few years ago, they debuted ‘Instant Raw’, which never worked. More recently they’ve released ‘Process Zero’, which is essentially their opinionated version of RAW with limitations. IMO, it results in worse images with no benefits. Finally, they have ‘Image Lab’, which is merely an exposure adjustment. One of the founders of Halide has a personal website in which he charges up to $1500 per month for access to a photography course, premium articles, and limited merch drops. Thus far, he hasn’t delivered on any of the aforementioned promises.

And $10 per month for an iPhone photo app is asinine.

reviews.title: Still not impressed with focus
reviews.review: Ive had halide for a long time now. Though there have been upgrades and improvements to the app, I still remain underwhelmed by the app. In the latest update, the focus brackets got even larger than before. Too many times I’ve touched to focus and the object I wanted to capture was not in focus, an object in front of what I wanted was in focus. This is because the focus are is way to broad. I don’t understand why the focus area can’t be reduced. The default camera app on the iPhone focus bracket is good but it could be more focused & smaller. The app Luwian has a nice focus point, ya’ll should try to match that apps focus. Now that the focus brackets are much larger, this is a problem for me. Focus peeking is functional, but the highlight area is to broad, almost everything is covered in green. I don’t think I’m going to continue to fund halide. The updates are noticeable but not dramatic. Now with the upcoming Mark III, I can’t shoot raw only, now a JPEG file gets saved & I have to CHOOSE the DNG file and manually export it… I don’t want to do that! An option for raw only is not available in settings. I don’t use Halide much at all, I’ve lost interest in the app.

reviews.title: 👎 Poor Zoom Usability
reviews.review:
Halide only allows rigid zoom steps (0.5× / 1× / 2× / 5×). A pro App should offer smooth zoom control for precise framing, even when staying within optical limits.

A simple preview-only zoom dial (no digital interpolation, no quality loss) would greatly improve usability. This feels like a design choice, not a limitation.

Great photos, frustrating experience.

reviews.title: Annoying
reviews.review: The exposure slide on the right and what you see is not correct. You’ll take a photo at flat 0.0, RAW, and then when it saves it, it’s either super blown out or super dark. I’ve tested in similar shots and it’s a coin flip on which way it automatically processes.

reviews.title: Refreshingly simple
reviews.review:
I like to use a camera. I like to figure out how to use it, with the light I have in front of me, to make art. iPhone camera app? Incredibly lifelike and functional photos in an instant. Document and move on. Halide is like having a high end digicam on you. To really get to know the lens. With a little adjustment you can barely tell it was taken on an iPhone. Apple algorithm, I can spot that look from 5 aisles back. 
Lifetime price is a good deal, for how long I’ll be using this app. Excited to see what other pro camera functions get ported over eventually.

reviews.title: Wish images saved in background
reviews.review:
I love Halide because of the Zero Process option. I really don’t like the Apple’s computational photography since the iPhone 11, so the Zero Process is a good return to what photos should look like

I just wish images saved in the background when the app is closed. Sometimes I’ll snap a picture of something and close the app, but then I won’t see it a few hours or days later in my photos app because Halide requires time to save photos while the app is open. This makes looking back on photos chronologically not great because the pictures don’t have the proper time they were taken. I don’t know if this problem extends to the location metadata too only being saved upon reopening the app

reviews.title: Masters of Marketing Comms & Cons
reviews.review:
This dev shop is adept at coming up with clever marketing terms for features that are mere gimmicks. A few years ago, they debuted ‘Instant Raw’, which never worked. More recently they’ve released ‘Process Zero’, which is essentially their opinionated version of RAW with limitations. IMO, it results in worse images with no benefits. Finally, they have ‘Image Lab’, which is merely an exposure adjustment. One of the founders of Halide has a personal website in which he charges up to $1500 per month for access to a photography course, premium articles, and limited merch drops. Thus far, he hasn’t delivered on any of the aforementioned promises.

And $10 per month for an iPhone photo app is asinine.

reviews.title: 👎 Poor Zoom Usability
reviews.review:
Halide only allows rigid zoom steps (0.5× / 1× / 2× / 5×). A pro App should offer smooth zoom control for precise framing, even when staying within optical limits.

A simple preview-only zoom dial (no digital interpolation, no quality loss) would greatly improve usability. This feels like a design choice, not a limitation.

Great photos, frustrating experience.

reviews.title: Annoying
reviews.review: The exposure slide on the right and what you see is not correct. You’ll take a photo at flat 0.0, RAW, and then when it saves it, it’s either super blown out or super dark. I’ve tested in similar shots and it’s a coin flip on which way it automatically processes.

reviews.title: Refreshingly simple
reviews.review:
I like to use a camera. I like to figure out how to use it, with the light I have in front of me, to make art. iPhone camera app? Incredibly lifelike and functional photos in an instant. Document and move on. Halide is like having a high end digicam on you. To really get to know the lens. With a little adjustment you can barely tell it was taken on an iPhone. Apple algorithm, I can spot that look from 5 aisles back. 
Lifetime price is a good deal, for how long I’ll be using this app. Excited to see what other pro camera functions get ported over eventually.

reviews.title: Wish images saved in background
reviews.review:
I love Halide because of the Zero Process option. I really don’t like the Apple’s computational photography since the iPhone 11, so the Zero Process is a good return to what photos should look like

I just wish images saved in the background when the app is closed. Sometimes I’ll snap a picture of something and close the app, but then I won’t see it a few hours or days later in my photos app because Halide requires time to save photos while the app is open. This makes looking back on photos chronologically not great because the pictures don’t have the proper time they were taken. I don’t know if this problem extends to the location metadata too only being saved upon reopening the app

reviews.title: Masters of Marketing Comms & Cons
reviews.review:
This dev shop is adept at coming up with clever marketing terms for features that are mere gimmicks. A few years ago, they debuted ‘Instant Raw’, which never worked. More recently they’ve released ‘Process Zero’, which is essentially their opinionated version of RAW with limitations. IMO, it results in worse images with no benefits. Finally, they have ‘Image Lab’, which is merely an exposure adjustment. One of the founders of Halide has a personal website in which he charges up to $1500 per month for access to a photography course, premium articles, and limited merch drops. Thus far, he hasn’t delivered on any of the aforementioned promises.

And $10 per month for an iPhone photo app is asinine.

reviews.title: Masters of Marketing Comms & Cons
reviews.review:
This dev shop is adept at coming up with clever marketing terms for features that are mere gimmicks. A few years ago, they debuted ‘Instant Raw’, which never worked. More recently they’ve released ‘Process Zero’, which is essentially their opinionated version of RAW with limitations. IMO, it results in worse images with no benefits. Finally, they have ‘Image Lab’, which is merely an exposure adjustment. One of the founders of Halide has a personal website in which he charges up to $1500 per month for access to a photography course, premium articles, and limited merch drops. Thus far, he hasn’t delivered on any of the aforementioned promises.

And $10 per month for an iPhone photo app is asinine.

Though there have been upgrades and improvements to the app, I still remain underwhelmed by the app. In the latest update, the focus brackets got even larger than before. Too many times I’ve touched to focus and the object I wanted to capture was not in focus, an object in front of what I wanted was in focus. This is because the focus are is way to broad. I don’t understand why the focus area can’t be reduced. The default camera app on the iPhone focus bracket is good but it could be more focused & smaller. The app Luwian has a nice focus point, ya’ll should try to match that apps focus. Now that the focus brackets are much larger, this is a problem for me. Focus peeking is functional, but the highlight area is to broad, almost everything is covered in green. I don’t think I’m going to continue to fund halide. The updates are noticeable but not dramatic. Now with the upcoming Mark III, I can’t shoot raw only, now a JPEG file gets saved & I have to CHOOSE the DNG file and manually export it… I don’t want to do that! An option for raw only is not available in settings. I don’t use Halide much at all, I’ve lost interest in the app.

reviews.title: Great for shooting DSLR kind of photos
reviews.review:
Native camera app is almost fully automatic. It is great in most scenarios. But it has restrains under certain situation like low ambient light. That’s where this app shines. I just came back from a vacation in Greece. I took many photos during dinner, where I wanted to avoid using flash for the sake of image quality and other guests. This app gave me complete control over shutter speed, ISO and depth to make it possible. I hand-held my iPhone, so shutter speed had to be faster than 1/8 at least. It would be impossible to control this with native app I think.
Another great example is controlling depth. I take photos of small insects and plants. Native camera app would always mess up the depth with auto focusing. (I don’t blame it btw. It’s called auto focusing after all.😅) While this app has like laser coloring to mark out the objects in focus. It is precise enough for my use. I found it actually more convenient than using my DSRL for such close-up shots.
All in all, a very nice free app gives me DSLR camera experience!

reviews.title: Great for shooting DSLR kind of photos
reviews.review:
Native camera app is almost fully automatic. It is great in most scenarios. But it has restrains under certain situation like low ambient light. That’s where this app shines. I just came back from a vacation in Greece. I took many photos during dinner, where I wanted to avoid using flash for the sake of image quality and other guests. This app gave me complete control over shutter speed, ISO and depth to make it possible. I hand-held my iPhone, so shutter speed had to be faster than 1/8 at least. It would be impossible to control this with native app I think.
Another great example is controlling depth. I take photos of small insects and plants. Native camera app would always mess up the depth with auto focusing. (I don’t blame it btw. It’s called auto focusing after all.😅) While this app has like laser coloring to mark out the objects in focus. It is precise enough for my use. I found it actually more convenient than using my DSRL for such close-up shots.
All in all, a very nice free app gives me DSLR camera experience!

reviews.title: Great for shooting DSLR kind of photos
reviews.review:
Native camera app is almost fully automatic. It is great in most scenarios. But it has restrains under certain situation like low ambient light. That’s where this app shines. I just came back from a vacation in Greece. I took many photos during dinner, where I wanted to avoid using flash for the sake of image quality and other guests. This app gave me complete control over shutter speed, ISO and depth to make it possible. I hand-held my iPhone, so shutter speed had to be faster than 1/8 at least. It would be impossible to control this with native app I think.
Another great example is controlling depth. I take photos of small insects and plants. Native camera app would always mess up the depth with auto focusing. (I don’t blame it btw. It’s called auto focusing after all.😅) While this app has like laser coloring to mark out the objects in focus. It is precise enough for my use. I found it actually more convenient than using my DSRL for such close-up shots.
All in all, a very nice free app gives me DSLR camera experience!

reviews.title: The greatest thing since sliced of bread

Who would’ve thought only Adobe that we could edit photos on the go on our smart phones, which are certainly smarter because of all the work that fabulous software companies like Adobe do to enhance our photo experience.
I’m an older guy now who is so thrilled at the direction that photography and image making has taken with all the digital advances and the wonderful ability to be able to control things that were only on the purview of labs before digital came along back in the film day. 
Don’t get me wrong there have been some wonderful labs over the years that we depended on and perhaps in many ways it lighten our workload because they did the hard part of dressing up all of our images and making them look very good. reviews.review: It’s been progressively getting worse. The amount of crashes and endless looping has become more and more frequent. I shouldn’t have to rely on an Internet connection to use a photo editor. I’ve used Photoshop for decades, literally, and this particular app used to be stellar. But the integration of iCloud has made it next to impossible to stabilize the app for use. I use this app every day and it has become more of a bother than a photo editor utility. And yes, I am a subscriber…

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.review:
This app used to be feasible for quick lower quality phone image edits, but turning even spot healing into a premium feature (it wasn’t before) is ridiculous, uninstalling.

EDIT:
I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.

reviews.title: The greatest thing since sliced of bread
reviews.review:
Who would’ve thought only Adobe that we could edit photos on the go on our smart phones, which are certainly smarter because of all the work that fabulous software companies like Adobe do to enhance our photo experience.
I’m an older guy now who is so thrilled at the direction that photography and image making has taken with all the digital advances and the wonderful ability to be able to control things that were only on the purview of labs before digital came along back in the film day. 
Don’t get me wrong there have been some wonderful labs over the years that we depended on and perhaps in many ways it lighten our workload because they did the hard part of dressing up all of our images and making them look very good.  But there was always something missing in the area of personal control that we now have due to Photoshop Lightroom Photoshop express all the things that make our image pop. So Adobe thank you.
Sincerely, Norman Dickson
Dickson Photography Jonesboro, Arkansas

reviews.title: Ever since this became a cloud app…
reviews.review: It’s been progressively getting worse. The amount of crashes and endless looping has become more and more frequent. I shouldn’t have to rely on an Internet connection to use a photo editor. I’ve used Photoshop for decades, literally, and this particular app used to be stellar. But the integration of iCloud has made it next to impossible to stabilize the app for use. I use this app every day and it has become more of a bother than a photo editor utility. And yes, I am a subscriber…

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.review:
This app used to be feasible for quick lower quality phone image edits, but turning even spot healing into a premium feature (it wasn’t before) is ridiculous, uninstalling.

EDIT:
I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.

reviews.review:
Who would’ve thought only Adobe that we could edit photos on the go on our smart phones, which are certainly smarter because of all the work that fabulous software companies like Adobe do to enhance our photo experience.

reviews.title: Ever since this became a cloud app…
reviews.review: It’s been progressively getting worse. The amount of crashes and endless looping has become more and more frequent. I shouldn’t have to rely on an Internet connection to use a photo editor. I’ve used Photoshop for decades, literally, and this particular app used to be stellar. But the integration of iCloud has made it next to impossible to stabilize the app for use. I use this app every day and it has become more of a bother than a photo editor utility. And yes, I am a subscriber…

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.review:
This app used to be feasible for quick lower quality phone image edits, but turning even spot healing into a premium feature (it wasn’t before) is ridiculous, uninstalling.

EDIT:
I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.

I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.

reviews.title: I Like my Real Face Better
reviews.review:
5 years ago, I used this app because I couldn’t stand the way my face looked in photos. 

Today I used the “more handsome” filter on a headshot and realized I like my real face better. 

The effects are a bit uncanny, and I don’t see the point in sharing a photo that doesn’t look like me. If I’m going to meet someone eventually, which is the goal, they’ll realize what I really look like. 

I feel like sharing a “fake” photo will only make my self esteem worse. I think that holds true for everyone. You deserve to be accepted for who you really are, and ultimately that’s only way you’ll feel better about yourself. 


However the lighting adjustments were nice and it was helpful for covering up a stupid zit I have on my nose atm. So the app is okay, I’d just recommend avoiding heavy filters.

reviews.title: I Like my Real Face Better
reviews.review:
5 years ago, I used this app because I couldn’t stand the way my face looked in photos. 

Today I used the “more handsome” filter on a headshot and realized I like my real face better. 

The effects are a bit uncanny, and I don’t see the point in sharing a photo that doesn’t look like me. If I’m going to meet someone eventually, which is the goal, they’ll realize what I really look like. 

I feel like sharing a “fake” photo will only make my self esteem worse. I think that holds true for everyone. You deserve to be accepted for who you really are, and ultimately that’s only way you’ll feel better about yourself. 


However the lighting adjustments were nice and it was helpful for covering up a stupid zit I have on my nose atm. So the app is okay, I’d just recommend avoiding heavy filters.

reviews.title: I Like my Real Face Better
reviews.review:
5 years ago, I used this app because I couldn’t stand the way my face looked in photos. 

Today I used the “more handsome” filter on a headshot and realized I like my real face better. 

The effects are a bit uncanny, and I don’t see the point in sharing a photo that doesn’t look like me. If I’m going to meet someone eventually, which is the goal, they’ll realize what I really look like. 

I feel like sharing a “fake” photo will only make my self esteem worse. I think that holds true for everyone. You deserve to be accepted for who you really are, and ultimately that’s only way you’ll feel better about yourself. 


However the lighting adjustments were nice and it was helpful for covering up a stupid zit I have on my nose atm. So the app is okay, I’d just recommend avoiding heavy filters.

reviews.title: Unauthorized charges over and over!
reviews.review: After trying the free trial and canceling the membership a very long time ago, I was still charged $84.39 for a “yearly subscription.” Apple refused to reimburse the charges and wouldn’t do anything about it. Under my apps it showed there wasn’t an active subscription. Months later, this charge tried being withdrawn again from several bank accounts I had connected with my Apple account over the years. I had to put a block on them. Here we are months later AGAIN and the charge tried being withdrawn from each account. The amount of $84.39 was taken from the 1 bank account that wasn’t blocked. There isn’t a way to contact the company/customer service when you can’t go through the app. I’m very upset and would not give any stars if I didn’t have to. Hopefully they make it right!

An easy 5 Star rating.

reviews.title: Perfect but limited.
reviews.review:
I thought I had found the perfect delayed shutter app, but I was so disappointed to find that the sequential delay is limited to only one second.
I would give it 5 stars if the delay between shots could be set to a higher range, such as x minutes. Nice app otherwise.

reviews.title: Simple Burst Camera - Nice!
reviews.review:
Great for group photos. I set my camera up for 4 shots, with a 0.5 second gap between each.  Later, I pick the best one.  

The camera also features an optional auto-flash and optional countdown timer - so you can get in the photo if you wish. 

The design of this camera has improved with updates and is pretty much perfect now, for what it does.  
An easy 5 Star rating.

reviews.title: Live Photos lack audio
reviews.review:
This is an amazing app! Extra points for having a lifetime purchase option. However, I will not be using this app beyond the free trial as Live Photos unfortunately do not have audio playback. This is a huge dealbreaker for me as I love playing back the Live Photos I take of my beautiful girlfriend.

Accessing the selfie camera is also incredibly unintuitive. Instead of having a standalone selfie button, you have to press the zoom button on the bottom right and THEN press the selfie button. While this may be a benefit for users focused on traditional photography, it’s an unnecessary extra step for me.

As such, the only option I have is Varlens which includes audio playback for Live Photos and a dedicated selfie button. 


Should the developer respond with any corrections or information of new update features, I will do my best to update my review!


While I personally won’t be using this app, I can definitely say that it’s a great app.

reviews.title: Love the interface, hate subscriptions
reviews.review:
I’ve been looking for something to replace FilmMic Pro since it had gone to a subscription model and rediscovered Obscura. I like the interface, very accessible even for new users. However, for advanced users or anyone looking for video, you’ll have to cough up more bucks to get to the “Pro” features. Once again, subscription raises its ugly head. 

I understand why people use it, but my issue is that these models tend to trap you by holding your media hostage if you decide not to renew, or they use some other way to keep you paying. Here the developer teases. Want to record video? You gotta pay. Want access to Raw? You gotta pay. Want to do anything beyond taking a snapshot? Pay up. I’d rather pay for versions and decide if upgrading to the latest is worth it. Guess I’ll keep looking.

reviews.title: Quickly becoming my go-to mobile photography app.
reviews.review: I've been on iOS since iOS 11, using an iPhone 6, and currently I''m on iOS 16, using an iPhone 13. During that time I've purchased, downloaded and used many apps in the category of mobile photography and still have a folder loaded with them. I make an effort to bounce between different ones, giving each a chance to stand out to me, especially after an update. Typically my favorites are Pro Shot and Halide, and Obscura was more or less an impulse buy at the time, which sat on my homescreen exactly where it downloaded to. But once I took the time to try it out I was surprised I hadn't gotten it sooner. Easy UI, flexible controls and great photo processing have made Obscura the app I keep finding myself gravitating towards everytime I see a shot I want to take. I own DSLR's and am amazed by how far mobile photography has evolved especially on iPhones - and I believe the team with Obscura is utilizing every bit of technological innovations to not only emulate DSLR grade photography, but to exceed and stand in a category it's own. Amazing job to the developers! Carpe Diem

reviews.title: Live Photos lack audio
reviews.review:
This is an amazing app! Extra points for having a lifetime purchase option. However, I will not be using this app beyond the free trial as Live Photos unfortunately do not have audio playback. This is a huge dealbreaker for me as I love playing back the Live Photos I take of my beautiful girlfriend.

Accessing the selfie camera is also incredibly unintuitive. Instead of having a standalone selfie button, you have to press the zoom button on the bottom right and THEN press the selfie button. While this may be a benefit for users focused on traditional photography, it’s an unnecessary extra step for me.

As such, the only option I have is Varlens which includes audio playback for Live Photos and a dedicated selfie button. 


Should the developer respond with any corrections or information of new update features, I will do my best to update my review!

reviews.title: Love the interface, hate subscriptions
reviews.review:
I’ve been looking for something to replace FilmMic Pro since it had gone to a subscription model and rediscovered Obscura. I like the interface, very accessible even for new users. However, for advanced users or anyone looking for video, you’ll have to cough up more bucks to get to the “Pro” features. Once again, subscription raises its ugly head. 

I understand why people use it, but my issue is that these models tend to trap you by holding your media hostage if you decide not to renew, or they use some other way to keep you paying. Here the developer teases. Want to record video? You gotta pay. Want access to Raw? You gotta pay. Want to do anything beyond taking a snapshot? Pay up. I’d rather pay for versions and decide if upgrading to the latest is worth it. Guess I’ll keep looking.

reviews.title: Quickly becoming my go-to mobile photography app.
reviews.review: I've been on iOS since iOS 11, using an iPhone 6, and currently I''m on iOS 16, using an iPhone 13. During that time I've purchased, downloaded and used many apps in the category of mobile photography and still have a folder loaded with them. I make an effort to bounce between different ones, giving each a chance to stand out to me, especially after an update. Typically my favorites are Pro Shot and Halide, and Obscura was more or less an impulse buy at the time, which sat on my homescreen exactly where it downloaded to. But once I took the time to try it out I was surprised I hadn't gotten it sooner. Easy UI, flexible controls and great photo processing have made Obscura the app I keep finding myself gravitating towards everytime I see a shot I want to take. I own DSLR's and am amazed by how far mobile photography has evolved especially on iPhones - and I believe the team with Obscura is utilizing every bit of technological innovations to not only emulate DSLR grade photography, but to exceed and stand in a category it's own. Amazing job to the developers! Carpe Diem

reviews.title: Professional Features, Easy to Use
reviews.review: As an educator, I love using Obscura Pro to demonstrate advanced photography techniques. The clean interface and powerful tools make it perfect for classroom workshops. ideal for STEM projects. Students can experiment with manual camera settings, lighting, and depth of field, making learning interactive and fun.

reviews.title: Live Photos lack audio
reviews.review:
This is an amazing app! Extra points for having a lifetime purchase option. However, I will not be using this app beyond the free trial as Live Photos unfortunately do not have audio playback. This is a huge dealbreaker for me as I love playing back the Live Photos I take of my beautiful girlfriend.

Accessing the selfie camera is also incredibly unintuitive. Instead of having a standalone selfie button, you have to press the zoom button on the bottom right and THEN press the selfie button. While this may be a benefit for users focused on traditional photography, it’s an unnecessary extra step for me.

As such, the only option I have is Varlens which includes audio playback for Live Photos and a dedicated selfie button. 


Should the developer respond with any corrections or information of new update features, I will do my best to update my review!


While I personally won’t be using this app, I can definitely say that it’s a great app.

As such, the only option I have is Varlens which includes audio playback for Live Photos and a dedicated selfie button.

reviews.title: ❤️INCREDIBLE….DREAM COME TRUE
reviews.review:
I’ve been doing photography for six years now, and for the longest time the workflow was always the same: take the photos off my camera or iPhone, move them to my computer, edit in Lightroom, Luminar, or another program, then export them again to an SSD or send them back to my iPhone so I could finally share them.

That whole process was long, tedious, and honestly took a lot of the fun out of editing.

After experiencing Darkroom, everything changed. Being able to edit directly from my camera roll, copy those edits, batch apply them to multiple photos, and have the originals replaced cleanly instead of dealing with extra copies or unnecessary complications feels incredible.

It made the workflow simple, fast, and enjoyable again. What used to take multiple steps across different devices can now be done in one smooth process right on my phone.

Another huge reason I appreciate this app is that I hate subscriptions. It’s refreshing to see that I can buy lifetime access instead of being locked into another monthly payment. Even better, the lifetime option costs less than the price of Adobe Lightroom, which makes it an easy value comparison for anyone serious about editing.

For anyone who values efficiency, quality, and a clean editing experience, this app is a game changer.

This is a dream come true. Ten out of ten. Honestly, very happy.

reviews.title: ❤️INCREDIBLE….DREAM COME TRUE
reviews.review:
I’ve been doing photography for six years now, and for the longest time the workflow was always the same: take the photos off my camera or iPhone, move them to my computer, edit in Lightroom, Luminar, or another program, then export them again to an SSD or send them back to my iPhone so I could finally share them.

That whole process was long, tedious, and honestly took a lot of the fun out of editing.

After experiencing Darkroom, everything changed. Being able to edit directly from my camera roll, copy those edits, batch apply them to multiple photos, and have the originals replaced cleanly instead of dealing with extra copies or unnecessary complications feels incredible.

It made the workflow simple, fast, and enjoyable again. What used to take multiple steps across different devices can now be done in one smooth process right on my phone.

Another huge reason I appreciate this app is that I hate subscriptions. It’s refreshing to see that I can buy lifetime access instead of being locked into another monthly payment. Even better, the lifetime option costs less than the price of Adobe Lightroom, which makes it an easy value comparison for anyone serious about editing.

For anyone who values efficiency, quality, and a clean editing experience, this app is a game changer.

This is a dream come true. Ten out of ten. Honestly, very happy.

reviews.title: ❤️INCREDIBLE….DREAM COME TRUE
reviews.review:
I’ve been doing photography for six years now, and for the longest time the workflow was always the same: take the photos off my camera or iPhone, move them to my computer, edit in Lightroom, Luminar, or another program, then export them again to an SSD or send them back to my iPhone so I could finally share them.

That whole process was long, tedious, and honestly took a lot of the fun out of editing.

After experiencing Darkroom, everything changed. Being able to edit directly from my camera roll, copy those edits, batch apply them to multiple photos, and have the originals replaced cleanly instead of dealing with extra copies or unnecessary complications feels incredible.

It made the workflow simple, fast, and enjoyable again. What used to take multiple steps across different devices can now be done in one smooth process right on my phone.

Another huge reason I appreciate this app is that I hate subscriptions. It’s refreshing to see that I can buy lifetime access instead of being locked into another monthly payment. Even better, the lifetime option costs less than the price of Adobe Lightroom, which makes it an easy value comparison for anyone serious about editing.

For anyone who values efficiency, quality, and a clean editing experience, this app is a game changer.

This is a dream come true. Ten out of ten. Honestly, very happy.

After experiencing Darkroom, everything changed. Being able to edit directly from my camera roll, copy those edits, batch apply them to multiple photos, and have the originals replaced cleanly instead of dealing with extra copies or unnecessary complications feels incredible.

It made the workflow simple, fast, and enjoyable again. What used to take multiple steps across different devices can now be done in one smooth process right on my phone.

Another huge reason I appreciate this app is that I hate subscriptions. It’s refreshing to see that I can buy lifetime access instead of being locked into another monthly payment. Even better, the lifetime option costs less than the price of Adobe Lightroom, which makes it an easy value comparison for anyone serious about editing.

For anyone who values efficiency, quality, and a clean editing experience, this app is a game changer.

This is a dream come true. Ten out of ten. Honestly, very happy.

EDIT:
I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.

reviews.title: The greatest thing since sliced of bread
reviews.review:
Who would’ve thought only Adobe that we could edit photos on the go on our smart phones, which are certainly smarter because of all the work that fabulous software companies like Adobe do to enhance our photo experience.
I’m an older guy now who is so thrilled at the direction that photography and image making has taken with all the digital advances and the wonderful ability to be able to control things that were only on the purview of labs before digital came along back in the film day. 
Don’t get me wrong there have been some wonderful labs over the years that we depended on and perhaps in many ways it lighten our workload because they did the hard part of dressing up all of our images and making them look very good.  But there was always something missing in the area of personal control that we now have due to Photoshop Lightroom Photoshop express all the things that make our image pop. So Adobe thank you.
Sincerely, Norman Dickson
Dickson Photography Jonesboro, Arkansas

reviews.title: Worst app on the App Store.

reviews.title: Ever since this became a cloud app…
reviews.review: It’s been progressively getting worse. The amount of crashes and endless looping has become more and more frequent. I shouldn’t have to rely on an Internet connection to use a photo editor. I’ve used Photoshop for decades, literally, and this particular app used to be stellar. But the integration of iCloud has made it next to impossible to stabilize the app for use. I use this app every day and it has become more of a bother than a photo editor utility. And yes, I am a subscriber…

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.review:
This app used to be feasible for quick lower quality phone image edits, but turning even spot healing into a premium feature (it wasn’t before) is ridiculous, uninstalling.

EDIT:
I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.

But the integration of iCloud has made it next to impossible to stabilize the app for use. I use this app every day and it has become more of a bother than a photo editor utility. And yes, I am a subscriber…

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.review:
This app used to be feasible for quick lower quality phone image edits, but turning even spot healing into a premium feature (it wasn’t before) is ridiculous, uninstalling.

EDIT:
I didn’t uninstall like I said I would above, and since then the app has gotten even worse - every photo I edit now has a QR code in the corner. The photo editing features this app still has for free aren’t worth that at all.
I recognize that some apps and programs aren’t supposed to be free. I’ve paid for may Adobe products. 
But this app used to have A LOT more features available for free and the QR code in the corner is a real deal breaker. I think this is a part of a larger pattern of Adobe lowering the quality of their products while charging more to subsidize their integration of AI tools that the majority of their customer base didn’t ask for.
As a long term Adobe customer, having paid for Photoshop and Lightroom products and creative cloud subscriptions over the past 15 years, I think I’m finally done.
